components.purpose: Shared Linux/Windows in-process game window, existing menus and Qt-owned Vulkan surface; SDL remains the controller/audio layer. The iced installer is separate.
components.qualification: Public release remains unqualified. The user explicitly approved isolated extraction/execution of the four existing verified archives for a game-launch MVP, deferring package-manager organization. The actual shared Qt runtime compiles with Qt 6.12.0 and paired LLVM-MinGW 22.1.7 in work/windows-tools/qt-mvp-6.12.0; the existing 23.1.4 toolchain is unchanged. The private receipt checks actual headers, libQt6Core/Gui/Widgets.a import libraries, DLL/plugin closure, paired compiler identity and source license texts. Qt's runtime-reference DLLs match the paired compiler's byte-for-byte; only one provider is used. The existing shaderc/FFmpeg compile/link/codec/relocation probe also passes with the paired compiler/runtime. The real user-selected game/update linked and launched with Qt's Windows plugin and Vulkan on an RTX2080Ti; a 60-second rerun after fixing GPU-importable guest backing visibly renders Rowan. These are not whole-game/ABI/Windows10 acceptance. Complete notices/source/build correspondence and redistribution review remain separate. The official Windows 10 1809+ baseline is not physical acceptance of the LLVM kit. No package manager, extra download or global toolchain switch was authorized. MSVC/GCC Qt binaries are not interchangeable C++ ABIs. The retained private SDL frontend is a diagnostic fallback, not acceptance of the common Qt game host.

release_blockers: LLVM-MinGW 20261020 and Unicorn 2.1.4 passed native generator probes after consented private preparation. Full dependency inventories, redistribution notices and Windows 10 qualification remain incomplete; GUI dependency downloads are not enabled.

Offline license evidence audit: preserve all LLVM host-tool notices, not just LICENSE.TXT. BusyBox is GPLv2, Make/gendef include GPLv3, and widl/Python/libffi have separate notices; matching copyleft host-tool source/build evidence is not locally supplied. The required CPython 3.13.15 archive/runtime is not locally available, and the compiler's Python 3.14 is not a substitute. Unicorn wheel metadata says BSD while its embedded README says GPLv2; full engine license/source qualification and authorized VC-runtime redistribution remain open.

Source-built notice recipes now retain SPDX LICENSES directories, authorship and hactool's embedded cJSON/Unicode/LZ4 statements in separate inventoried private bundle variants. FFmpeg import can supplement generic GPLv3/LGPLv3 texts from the already pinned older source archive; these texts do not establish corresponding sources for the 8.1 binary or qualify transitive components. Preserving notices is not redistribution approval or proof of a license violation.

The repeated offline audit verifies the four existing Qt MVP archive pins, installed Qt receipt, 38 top-level Qt license texts against the approved source archive, and libc++/libunwind identity with the paired compiler. It inventories 93 third-party source notice/attribution candidates, not 93 confirmed deployed obligations. Qt's current private receipt does not itself bind the archive pins or a corresponding producer recipe; generic top-level license texts are not complete third-party attributions. The paired compiler retains 34 notice texts, but copyleft host-tool corresponding sources/build evidence and applicable deployed runtime notices remain release gates. No live package was changed or redistribution qualified.

The active amd64 runtime including Vulkan/VMA/SDL/movie compiles and links with synthetic guest tables, boots without developer PATH and reports host crashes. Actual shaderc SPIR-V/error probes and FFmpeg ABI/license/VP8 Unicode WebM roundtrip pass. SDL virtual controllers/dummy audio and ARM64 non-graphics cross-link also pass. These are not gameplay, GPU, physical audio/controllers, native ARM64, whole-game GC or IME acceptance.

An explicit debug-only local offline catalog now connects GUI prerequisites/build to extraction, C generation, full Vulkan/movie linking, packaging and transactional per-user installation. Native tests traverse real generation through relocated installation after synthetic extraction, plus the real isolated JSONL/native-extractor failure path. Real dump/keys selection through the GUI to a playable installation is not accepted. The public GUI gate remains closed.
Windows 10 22H2, Windows 11 and the USB/Bluetooth controller matrix require real hardware acceptance.
ARM64 is a separate experimental target; native host Unicorn and target dependencies/hardware are not qualified.
